authors: K. Lee, B. D. Eoff, and J. Caverlee
title: Seven months with the devils: A long-term study of content polluters on Twitter
venue: Proceedings of the International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM)
one_line_finding: Deployed 60 honeypot accounts for seven months, harvesting about 36,000 content polluters and analysing their links, behaviour and follower dynamics to build detection features.

authors: Z. Chu, S. Gianvecchio, H. Wang, and S. Jajodia
title: Detecting automation of Twitter accounts: Are you a human, bot, or cyborg?
venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
one_line_finding: Characterised human, bot and cyborg Twitter accounts and combined entropy of posting intervals, spam content, and account properties in a classifier to separate them.

authors: S. Cresci, R. Di Pietro, M. Petrocchi, A. Spognardi, and M. Tesconi
title: The paradigm-shift of social spambots: Evidence, theories, and tools for the arms race
venue: Proceedings of the 26th International Conference on World Wide Web Companion (WWW '17 Companion)
one_line_finding: Showed that a new generation of social spambots mimicking humans evades both platform moderation and established detectors, motivating group-level detection approaches.

authors: O. Varol, E. Ferrara, C. Davis, F. Menczer, and A. Flammini
title: Online human-bot interactions: Detection, estimation, and characterization
venue: Proceedings of the International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM)
one_line_finding: Built a detector over more than a thousand user, network, temporal, content and sentiment features and estimated that 9-15% of active Twitter accounts are bots.

authors: K.-C. Yang, O. Varol, P.-M. Hui, and F. Menczer
title: Scalable and generalizable social bot detection through data selection
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
one_line_finding: A lightweight metadata-only bot detector scales to the real-time Twitter stream; selecting a strategic training subset improves cross-domain generalization over training on all data.

authors: S. Kudugunta and E. Ferrara
title: Deep neural networks for bot detection
venue: Information Sciences
one_line_finding: Proposed a contextual LSTM combining tweet text and metadata, achieving high tweet-level bot detection accuracy and using SMOTE-style synthetic oversampling for account-level detection.

authors: E. Ferrara, O. Varol, C. Davis, F. Menczer, and A. Flammini
title: The rise of social bots
venue: Communications of the ACM
one_line_finding: Reviewed how increasingly sophisticated social bots threaten online ecosystems and surveyed graph-, crowdsourcing- and feature-based detection strategies.

authors: S. Cresci
title: A decade of social bot detection
venue: Communications of the ACM
one_line_finding: Reviewed ten years of bot detection, documenting the shift from individual to group-based and adversarial approaches as bots increasingly interfere with elections and markets.

authors: M. Sayyadiharikandeh, O. Varol, K.-C. Yang, A. Flammini, and F. Menczer
title: Detection of novel social bots by ensembles of specialized classifiers
venue: Proceedings of the 29th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
one_line_finding: Trained specialized classifiers per bot class and combined them via maximum-rule voting, improving generalization to unseen bot types over a single monolithic model.

authors: J. Echeverría, E. De Cristofaro, N. Kourtellis, I. Leontiadis, G. Stringhini, and S. Zhou
title: LOBO: Evaluation of generalization deficiencies in Twitter bot classifiers
venue: Proceedings of the 34th Annual Computer Security Applications Conference (ACSAC)
one_line_finding: Introduced leave-one-botnet-out evaluation and showed that bot classifiers trained on known botnets generalize poorly to unseen bot classes.

authors: C. Hays, Z. Schutzman, M. Raghavan, E. Walk, and P. Zimmer
title: Simplistic collection and labeling practices limit the utility of benchmark datasets for Twitter bot detection
venue: Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference (WWW)
one_line_finding: Showed that simple decision rules on few features nearly solve popular bot benchmarks, revealing that collection and labelling artefacts inflate reported accuracy and limit generalization.

authors: K.-C. Yang, E. Ferrara, and F. Menczer
title: Botometer 101: Social bot practicum for computational social scientists
venue: Journal of Computational Social Science
one_line_finding: Practical guide to Botometer explaining its supervised feature-based design, score interpretation, threshold choice and pitfalls when used in social science research.

authors: S. Feng, H. Wan, N. Wang, and M. Luo
title: BotRGCN: Twitter bot detection with relational graph convolutional networks
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/ACM International Conference on Advances in Social Networks Analysis and Mining (ASONAM)
one_line_finding: Built a heterogeneous follow graph with description, tweet and metadata features and applied relational GCNs, outperforming feature-based bot detectors on TwiBot-20.

authors: S. Feng, H. Wan, N. Wang, J. Li, and M. Luo
title: TwiBot-20: A comprehensive Twitter bot detection benchmark
venue: Proceedings of the 30th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
one_line_finding: Released a benchmark of about 230k Twitter users with tweets, metadata and follow relations spanning diverse topics, showing existing detectors struggle on its diverse bots.

authors: S. Feng et al.
title: TwiBot-22: Towards graph-based Twitter bot detection
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (NeurIPS 2022), Datasets and Benchmarks Track
one_line_finding: Introduced a large graph-based bot benchmark with richer entities and relations and better annotation, re-implementing 35 baselines across nine datasets.

authors: S. Feng, Z. Tan, R. Li, and M. Luo
title: Heterogeneity-aware Twitter bot detection with relational graph transformers
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
one_line_finding: Modelled relation and influence heterogeneity among users with relational graph transformers and semantic attention, improving bot detection on TwiBot-20.

authors: Y. Liu, Z. Tan, H. Wang, S. Feng, Q. Zheng, and M. Luo
title: BotMoE: Twitter bot detection with community-aware mixtures of modal-specific experts
venue: Proceedings of the 46th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
one_line_finding: Fused metadata, text and network experts through a community-aware mixture-of-experts layer, beating prior detectors on three benchmarks and generalizing to unseen communities.

authors: Z. Cai, Z. Tan, Z. Lei, Z. Zhu, H. Wang, Q. Zheng, and M. Luo
title: LMBot: Distilling graph knowledge into language model for graph-less deployment in Twitter bot detection
venue: Proceedings of the 17th ACM International Conference on Web Search and Data Mining (WSDM)
one_line_finding: Iteratively distilled knowledge between a graph neural network and a language model so the language model alone detects bots without graph data at deployment.

authors: Z. Tan, S. Feng, M. Sclar, H. Wan, M. Luo, Y. Choi, and Y. Tsvetkov
title: BotPercent: Estimating bot populations in Twitter communities
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2023
one_line_finding: Estimated community-level bot shares with confidence-calibrated multi-model detectors, giving less biased estimates and revealing heterogeneous bot presence across Twitter communities.

authors: Z. Lei, H. Wan, W. Zhang, S. Feng, Z. Chen, J. Li, Q. Zheng, and M. Luo
title: BIC: Twitter bot detection with text-graph interaction and semantic consistency
venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
one_line_finding: Let text and graph modalities exchange information through interaction layers and added a semantic-consistency signal capturing repetitive tweet content of bots.

authors: Y. Yang, Q. Wu, B. He, H. Peng, R. Yang, Z. Hao, and Y. Liao
title: SEBot: Structural entropy guided multi-view contrastive learning for social bot detection
venue: Proceedings of the 30th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
one_line_finding: Used structural entropy to encode hierarchical community structure and multi-view contrastive learning to make graph-based bot detection robust to heterophily.

authors: B. He et al.
title: Dynamicity-aware social bot detection with dynamic graph transformers
venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Third International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI)
one_line_finding: Modelled the evolving social graph with structural and temporal transformer modules, showing that capturing graph dynamics improves bot detection over static GNNs.

authors: J. Duan, W. Li, Q. Bai, M. Nguyen, X. Wang, and J. Jiang
title: LLM-BotGuard: A novel framework for detecting LLM-driven bots with mixture of experts and graph neural networks
venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems
one_line_finding: Combined feature extraction, a mixture-of-experts module and graph neural networks to detect LLM-driven social bots, outperforming baseline detectors.

authors: S. Feng, H. Wan, N. Wang, Z. Tan, M. Luo, and Y. Tsvetkov
title: What does the bot say? Opportunities and risks of large language models in social media bot detection
venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
one_line_finding: LLM-based mixture-of-heterogeneous-experts detectors tuned on 1,000 examples beat baselines by up to 9.1%, but LLM-guided manipulation cuts detector performance by up to 29.6% and harms calibration.

authors: B. Qiao, K. Li, W. Zhou, S. Li, Q. Lu, and S. Hu
title: BotSim: LLM-powered malicious social botnet simulation
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
one_line_finding: Simulated LLM-driven malicious botnets interacting with real users and released BotSim-24, on which detectors that succeed on traditional datasets perform poorly.

authors: S. Li, J. Yang, and K. Zhao
title: Are you in a masquerade? Exploring the behavior and impact of large language model driven social bots in online social networks
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2307.10337
one_line_finding: Studied LLM-driven bots on Chirper, finding stronger individual camouflage, group-level patterns and toxic community influence; released Masquerade-23 and found existing detectors only partly effective.

authors: K.-C. Yang and F. Menczer
title: Anatomy of an AI-powered malicious social botnet
venue: Journal of Quantitative Description: Digital Media
one_line_finding: Identified a botnet of 1,140 coordinated accounts apparently using ChatGPT to post human-like content; state-of-the-art LLM-content classifiers failed to separate them from humans.

authors: E. Ferrara
title: Social bot detection in the age of ChatGPT: Challenges and opportunities
venue: First Monday
one_line_finding: Reviewed bot detection amid generative chatbots and called for generative-agent synthetic data, multimodal cross-platform detection, low-resource languages and privacy-preserving learning.

authors: F. Menczer, D. Crandall, Y.-Y. Ahn, and A. Kapadia
title: Addressing the harms of AI-generated inauthentic content
venue: Nature Machine Intelligence
one_line_finding: Commentary arguing that generative AI makes inauthentic content cheap and scalable, and outlining technical, platform and policy countermeasures against its harms.

authors: E. Ferrara
title: GenAI against humanity: Nefarious applications of generative artificial intelligence and large language models
venue: Journal of Computational Social Science
one_line_finding: Catalogued misuse of generative AI and LLMs, including deepfakes, synthetic identities, targeted scams and misinformation, urging preparedness against these risks.

authors: J. A. Goldstein, J. Chao, S. Grossman, A. Stamos, and M. Tomz
title: How persuasive is AI-generated propaganda?
venue: PNAS Nexus
one_line_finding: A survey experiment with US respondents found GPT-3 propaganda highly persuasive, and with prompt editing and curation about as persuasive as real propaganda.

authors: J. Duan, S. Wu, W. Li, Q. Bai, M. Nguyen, and J. Jiang
title: BotDMM: Dual-channel multi-modal learning for LLM-driven bot detection on social media
venue: Information Fusion
one_line_finding: Combined content and network-structure channels with self-supervised joint training to distinguish humans, traditional bots and LLM-driven bots.

authors: Z. Wang, Z. Lin, Z. Wang, and H. Wang
title: TRACE-Bot: Detecting emerging LLM-driven social bots via implicit semantic representations and AIGC-enhanced behavioral patterns
venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2604.02147
one_line_finding: Fused language-model representations with behavioural features enhanced by AI-generated-content detector outputs, reaching 98.46% and 97.50% accuracy on two LLM-bot datasets.

authors: S. Lopez-Joya, J. A. Diaz-Garcia, M. D. Ruiz, and M. J. Martin-Bautista
title: Dissecting a social bot powered by generative AI: Anatomy, new trends and challenges
venue: Social Network Analysis and Mining
one_line_finding: Reviewed generative-AI-era bot detection, proposed a bot categorisation, and used explainable AI to analyse datasets, classifiers and causes of misclassification.

authors: T. Fagni, F. Falchi, M. Gambini, A. Martella, and M. Tesconi
title: TweepFake: About detecting deepfake tweets
venue: PLOS ONE
one_line_finding: Released 25,572 real tweets, half from 23 bots imitating 17 humans via Markov chains, RNNs and GPT-2, and benchmarked 13 deepfake-tweet detectors.

authors: S. Gehrmann, H. Strobelt, and A. Rush
title: GLTR: Statistical detection and visualization of generated text
venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics: System Demonstrations
one_line_finding: Visualised token-rank statistics under a language model to expose generated text, raising untrained human detection accuracy from 54% to 72%.

authors: E. Mitchell, Y. Lee, A. Khazatsky, C. D. Manning, and C. Finn
title: DetectGPT: Zero-shot machine-generated text detection using probability curvature
venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR
one_line_finding: Showed LLM samples lie in negative-curvature regions of the log-probability function, enabling zero-shot detection that raised fake-news AUROC from 0.81 to 0.95.

authors: G. Bao, Y. Zhao, Z. Teng, L. Yang, and Y. Zhang
title: Fast-DetectGPT: Efficient zero-shot detection of machine-generated text via conditional probability curvature
venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)
one_line_finding: Replaced DetectGPT perturbations with sampling-based conditional probability curvature, giving about 75% relative improvement while running 340 times faster.

authors: A. Hans, A. Schwarzschild, V. Cherepanova, H. Kazemi, A. Saha, M. Goldblum, et al.
title: Spotting LLMs with Binoculars: Zero-shot detection of machine-generated text
venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR
one_line_finding: Contrasted perplexity and cross-perplexity of two related LLMs for training-free detection, flagging over 90% of ChatGPT text at a 0.01% false-positive rate.

authors: V. Verma, E. Fleisig, N. Tomlin, and D. Klein
title: Ghostbuster: Detecting text ghostwritten by large language models
venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the ACL: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)
one_line_finding: Trained a classifier on features from weaker language-model probabilities without target-model access, reaching 99.0 F1 and improving cross-domain generalization by 7.5 F1.

authors: X. Hu, P.-Y. Chen, and T.-Y. Ho
title: RADAR: Robust AI-text detection via adversarial learning
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (NeurIPS 2023)
one_line_finding: Adversarially trained a paraphraser and detector jointly, making detection robust to paraphrasing across eight LLMs and four datasets with good transfer.

authors: K. Krishna, Y. Song, M. Karpinska, J. Wieting, and M. Iyyer
title: Paraphrasing evades detectors of AI-generated text, but retrieval is an effective defense
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36 (NeurIPS 2023)
one_line_finding: The DIPPER paraphraser cut DetectGPT accuracy from 70.3% to 4.6% at 1% FPR, whereas retrieval over stored generations recovered 80-97% of paraphrases.

authors: J. Kirchenbauer, J. Geiping, Y. Wen, J. Katz, I. Miers, and T. Goldstein
title: A watermark for large language models
venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR
one_line_finding: Embedded a statistically detectable watermark by softly favouring a random green-token list during sampling, detectable without model access and with minimal quality impact.

authors: L. Dugan, A. Hwang, F. Trhlík, A. Zhu, J. M. Ludan, H. Xu, et al.
title: RAID: A shared benchmark for robust evaluation of machine-generated text detectors
venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
one_line_finding: Built a 6M-text benchmark over 11 models, 8 domains, 11 attacks and 4 decoding strategies; 12 detectors proved brittle to attacks, sampling changes and unseen models.

authors: Y. Wang et al.
title: M4: Multi-generator, multi-domain, and multi-lingual black-box machine-generated text detection
venue: Proceedings of the 18th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
one_line_finding: Released a multi-generator, multi-domain, multilingual benchmark showing detectors fail to generalize to unseen domains or LLMs and often label machine text as human.

authors: J. Wu, S. Yang, R. Zhan, Y. Yuan, L. S. Chao, and D. F. Wong
title: A survey on LLM-generated text detection: Necessity, methods, and future directions
venue: Computational Linguistics
one_line_finding: Surveyed watermarking, statistical, neural and human-assisted LLM-text detectors, datasets, and open challenges such as out-of-distribution data and adversarial attacks.

authors: A. Creo and S. Pudasaini
title: SilverSpeak: Evading AI-generated text detectors using homoglyphs
venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on GenAI Content Detection (GenAIDetect), co-located with COLING 2025
one_line_finding: Homoglyph substitution evaded seven AI-text detectors on five datasets, dropping average MCC from 0.64 to -0.01.

authors: D. Macko, J. Kopál, R. Moro, and I. Srba
title: MultiSocial: Multilingual benchmark of machine-generated text detection of social-media texts
venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
one_line_finding: Built a 472k-text benchmark across 22 languages and 5 platforms; fine-tuned detectors learn social-media text well and the training platform choice matters.

authors: D. Jin, Z. Jin, J. T. Zhou, and P. Szolovits
title: Is BERT really robust? A strong baseline for natural language attack on text classification and entailment
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
one_line_finding: Introduced TextFooler, a synonym-substitution black-box attack that fooled BERT and other models on classification and entailment while preserving semantics, in linear time.

authors: J. Li, S. Ji, T. Du, B. Li, and T. Wang
title: TextBugger: Generating adversarial text against real-world applications
venue: Proceedings of the Network and Distributed System Security Symposium (NDSS)
one_line_finding: Generated utility-preserving character- and word-level adversarial text that fooled white-box and black-box commercial sentiment and toxicity classifiers with high success rates.

authors: J. Gao, J. Lanchantin, M. L. Soffa, and Y. Qi
title: Black-box generation of adversarial text sequences to evade deep learning classifiers
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE Security and Privacy Workshops (SPW)
one_line_finding: Proposed DeepWordBug, scoring important tokens and applying small character edits that sharply reduced deep text classifier accuracy in a black-box setting.

authors: J. Ebrahimi, A. Rao, D. Lowd, and D. Dou
title: HotFlip: White-box adversarial examples for text classification
venue: Proceedings of the 56th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 2: Short Papers)
one_line_finding: Used gradients over one-hot inputs to choose character flips that fool a character-level classifier with few edits, enabling fast adversarial training.

authors: S. Eger, G. G. Şahin, A. Rücklé, J.-U. Lee, C. Schulz, M. Mesgar, et al.
title: Text processing like humans do: Visually attacking and shielding NLP systems
venue: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference of the North American Chapter of the ACL: Human Language Technologies, Volume 1
one_line_finding: Visually similar character substitutions degraded NLP models by up to 82% while humans read them easily; visual embeddings and adversarial training only partly restored robustness.

authors: N. Boucher, I. Shumailov, R. Anderson, and N. Papernot
title: Bad characters: Imperceptible NLP attacks
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
one_line_finding: Showed that invisible characters, homoglyphs, reorderings and deletions in Unicode encoding imperceptibly break commercial and open NLP systems, including toxic-content detectors.

authors: L. Li, R. Ma, Q. Guo, X. Xue, and X. Qiu
title: BERT-ATTACK: Adversarial attack against BERT using BERT
venue: Proceedings of the 2020 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)
one_line_finding: Used a masked language model to propose fluent substitutions that fool fine-tuned BERT with higher success and lower perturbation rates than prior attacks.

authors: L. Wang, X. Qiao, Y. Xie, W. Nie, Y. Zhang, and A. Liu
title: My brother helps me: Node injection based adversarial attack on social bot detection
venue: Proceedings of the 31st ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM)
one_line_finding: Injected new bot nodes near a target bot in black-box fashion, evading GNN bot detectors with over 73% success on Cresci-2015 and TwiBot-22.

authors: S. M. Lundberg and S.-I. Lee
title: A unified approach to interpreting model predictions
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NIPS 2017)
one_line_finding: Introduced SHAP, the unique additive feature attribution satisfying local accuracy, missingness and consistency, unifying six existing explanation methods.

authors: S. M. Lundberg, G. Erion, H. Chen, A. DeGrave, J. M. Prutkin, B. Nair, et al.
title: From local explanations to global understanding with explainable AI for trees
venue: Nature Machine Intelligence
one_line_finding: Presented TreeSHAP, a polynomial-time exact Shapley value algorithm for tree ensembles, plus interaction values and tools for building global understanding from local explanations.

authors: M. T. Ribeiro, S. Singh, and C. Guestrin
title: "Why should I trust you?": Explaining the predictions of any classifier
venue: Proceedings of the 22nd ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
one_line_finding: Proposed LIME, explaining any classifier's prediction by fitting an interpretable local surrogate model around the instance, and SP-LIME for selecting representative explanations.

authors: M. Sundararajan, A. Taly, and Q. Yan
title: Axiomatic attribution for deep networks
venue: Proceedings of the 34th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR
one_line_finding: Proposed Integrated Gradients, satisfying sensitivity and implementation invariance axioms that most prior attribution methods violate, using only a few gradient calls.

authors: A. Ghorbani, A. Abid, and J. Zou
title: Interpretation of neural networks is fragile
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
one_line_finding: Small crafted input perturbations that preserve the predicted label drastically change feature-importance and exemplar-based explanations on ImageNet and CIFAR-10.

authors: D. Slack, S. Hilgard, E. Jia, S. Singh, and H. Lakkaraju
title: Fooling LIME and SHAP: Adversarial attacks on post hoc explanation methods
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society (AIES)
one_line_finding: A scaffolding classifier that detects off-manifold perturbation queries hid biased behaviour from LIME and SHAP, yielding innocuous explanations for discriminatory models.

authors: A.-K. Dombrowski, M. Alber, C. Anders, M. Ackermann, K.-R. Müller, and P. Kessel
title: Explanations can be manipulated and geometry is to blame
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32 (NeurIPS 2019)
one_line_finding: Nearly imperceptible input changes arbitrarily manipulate explanations while outputs stay constant; the effect stems from network geometry and is bounded, motivating smoother explanations.

authors: S. Krishna, T. Han, A. Gu, S. Wu, S. Jabbari, and H. Lakkaraju
title: The disagreement problem in explainable machine learning: A practitioner's perspective
venue: Transactions on Machine Learning Research
one_line_finding: Through interviews and a quantitative framework, found post hoc explainers frequently disagree and practitioners resolve disagreement with ad hoc heuristics.

authors: W. Webber, A. Moffat, and J. Zobel
title: A similarity measure for indefinite rankings
venue: ACM Transactions on Information Systems
one_line_finding: Proposed rank-biased overlap, a top-weighted similarity for incomplete, non-conjoint rankings grounded in a probabilistic user model and monotonic in evaluation depth.

authors: P. W. Koh, T. Nguyen, Y. S. Tang, S. Mussmann, E. Pierson, B. Kim, and P. Liang
title: Concept bottleneck models
venue: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR
one_line_finding: Models first predict human-interpretable concepts and then the label, letting users inspect and intervene on concepts while staying competitive with end-to-end models.

authors: B. Kim, M. Wattenberg, J. Gilmer, C. Cai, J. Wexler, F. Viegas, and R. Sayres
title: Interpretability beyond feature attribution: Quantitative testing with concept activation vectors (TCAV)
venue: Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR
one_line_finding: Introduced concept activation vectors and TCAV, using directional derivatives to quantify how much a human-defined concept influences a network's predictions.

authors: C. Agarwal, S. Krishna, E. Saxena, M. Pawelczyk, N. Johnson, I. Puri, et al.
title: OpenXAI: Towards a transparent evaluation of model explanations
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (NeurIPS 2022), Datasets and Benchmarks Track
one_line_finding: Released an open benchmark with datasets, models and 22 metrics covering faithfulness, stability and fairness of post hoc explanations, with public leaderboards.

authors: A. Shevtsov, C. Tzagkarakis, D. Antonakaki, and S. Ioannidis
title: Identification of Twitter bots based on an explainable machine learning framework: The US 2020 elections case study
venue: Proceedings of the International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM)
one_line_finding: Detected Twitter bots with a tuned XGBoost model and used SHAP to explain feature importance, outperforming a recent state-of-the-art method on distinct datasets.

authors: O. Çitlak, İ. Atacak, and İ. A. Doğru
title: A novel approach to SPAM detection in social networks-Light-ANFIS: Integrating gradient-based one-sided sampling and random forest-based feature clustering techniques with adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference systems
venue: Applied Sciences
one_line_finding: Combined a neuro-fuzzy inference system with GOSS sampling and random-forest feature clustering for fast X spam detection, matching deep hybrids on three datasets.

authors: D. H. Wolpert
title: Stacked generalization
venue: Neural Networks
one_line_finding: Introduced stacking, training a higher-level generalizer on the cross-validated outputs of base generalizers to reduce generalization error.

authors: L. Breiman
title: Random forests
venue: Machine Learning
one_line_finding: Combined bagged decision trees with random feature selection at each split, showing generalization error converges and depends on tree strength and correlation.

authors: T. Chen and C. Guestrin
title: XGBoost: A scalable tree boosting system
venue: Proceedings of the 22nd ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
one_line_finding: Presented a regularised, sparsity-aware gradient tree boosting system with weighted quantile sketch and cache-aware, out-of-core computation that scales to billions of examples.

authors: G. Ke, Q. Meng, T. Finley, T. Wang, W. Chen, W. Ma, et al.
title: LightGBM: A highly efficient gradient boosting decision tree
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NIPS 2017)
one_line_finding: Gradient-based one-side sampling and exclusive feature bundling sped up gradient boosting by up to 20 times with nearly identical accuracy.

authors: R. A. Jacobs, M. I. Jordan, S. J. Nowlan, and G. E. Hinton
title: Adaptive mixtures of local experts
venue: Neural Computation
one_line_finding: Proposed a gating network that softly assigns inputs to competing expert networks, so experts specialise on subsets of cases, demonstrated on vowel discrimination.

authors: N. Shazeer, A. Mirhoseini, K. Maziarz, A. Davis, Q. V. Le, G. E. Hinton, and J. Dean
title: Outrageously large neural networks: The sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layer
venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)
one_line_finding: A sparsely gated mixture-of-experts layer with thousands of experts gave over 1000x capacity gains, improving language modelling and translation at lower compute cost.

authors: W. Fedus, B. Zoph, and N. Shazeer
title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to trillion parameter models with simple and efficient sparsity
venue: Journal of Machine Learning Research
one_line_finding: Simplified mixture-of-experts routing to a single expert per token, enabling stable, faster pre-training of trillion-parameter sparse language models.

authors: R. M. O. Cruz, R. Sabourin, and G. D. C. Cavalcanti
title: Dynamic classifier selection: Recent advances and perspectives
venue: Information Fusion
one_line_finding: Reviewed dynamic classifier and ensemble selection, proposing a taxonomy of region-of-competence definitions and selection criteria, and an empirical comparison of methods.

authors: A. H. R. Ko, R. Sabourin, and A. S. Britto, Jr.
title: From dynamic classifier selection to dynamic ensemble selection
venue: Pattern Recognition
one_line_finding: Proposed KNORA, selecting per test sample the ensemble of classifiers that correctly label its nearest validation neighbours, outperforming static and single-classifier selection.

authors: Y. Bilgen and M. Kaya
title: EGMA: Ensemble learning-based hybrid model approach for spam detection
venue: Applied Sciences
one_line_finding: Combined GRU, MLP and hybrid autoencoder models by majority voting with statistical and TF-IDF features, reaching up to 99.28% accuracy on SMS spam.

authors: C. Guo, G. Pleiss, Y. Sun, and K. Q. Weinberger
title: On calibration of modern neural networks
venue: Proceedings of the 34th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR
one_line_finding: Modern deep networks are poorly calibrated, influenced by depth, width, weight decay and batch normalisation, and simple temperature scaling fixes calibration on most datasets.

authors: V. Vovk, A. Gammerman, and G. Shafer

one_line_finding: Tutorial on split conformal prediction, conformal risk control and extensions to shift, with practical score functions and code for producing valid prediction sets.

title: Conformal risk control
venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)

venue: Journal of the ACM
